main.claim: Paste a YouTube link and get the full transcript of the video, word for word, with punctuation and paragraph breaks. Copy it with one click. Free: 3 runs a day, and 3 more after you leave an email. No account needed.

sections.heading: Get a YouTube transcript in four steps
sections.body:
Paste a link and the tool writes out what is said in the video. You do not install anything, and you do not need an account. The answer usually comes back in about 1 to 3 seconds for a short video. Longer videos take longer.

1. Copy the link to the YouTube video from your browser's address bar.
2. Open [YouTube Transcript](https://youtube-transcript.lazur.app/) and paste the link into the box.
3. Press the button and wait for the text to appear.
4. Press Copy to put the whole transcript on your clipboard.

sections.heading: What the transcript looks like
sections.body:
The text is written word for word, with punctuation and paragraph breaks. It is built for reading and searching. After you paste it into a page, press Ctrl+F (Command+F on a Mac) to find a name or a phrase inside it.

The output has paragraph breaks, not timestamps. The text does not tell you the minute each line was said, so if you need to find a moment in the video, search the text for the phrase and then watch the video from there.

**If the tool cannot access the speech in a video, it says so in one sentence.** You get that message instead of a transcript, so you know the tool did not finish the job.

sections.heading: Check the words before you quote them
sections.body:
The tool turns speech into text with AI, so it can get some words wrong. Names, product names, numbers, dates, and words spoken over music or a crowd are the most likely to be off. Before you quote a line, play that part of the video and compare it with the text.

For notes or a rough record, a quick read is often enough. For anything you publish or send to someone else, read the full transcript against the video at least once.

sections.heading: Free use and limits
sections.body:
This tool is free. You get 3 transcripts a day. After you leave an email, you get 3 more. You do not need an account to use the free runs, and results can be copied with one click.

These are the limits this tool sets today. If you plan to transcribe many videos, check the current limits before you build a routine around the tool.

sections.heading: What to do with the text
sections.body:
Copy the text into a document, a notes app, or a search box. Once it is in a page, Ctrl+F finds any word in seconds. Use the transcript to quote a speaker, to make notes from a lecture or interview, or to find a part of a long video you want to watch again.

If you need the main points rather than every word, use the [YouTube summarizer](https://youtube-summarizer.lazur.app/) instead. A summary is shorter, but it leaves out the exact wording.

sections.heading: What to look for in a transcript generator
sections.body:
Start with what you will do with the text. For notes, search matters most. For quoting someone, the exact wording and the check against the video matter most. For a video you want to find again, timestamps matter most.

- **Free use and limits.** Check how many transcripts you get, and whether you must sign up or leave an email.
- **Timestamps.** Useful if you want to jump back to a part of the video. Not every tool includes them.
- **Languages.** Check that the tool handles the language the video is spoken in.
- **Copy or download.** Make sure you can copy the text in one step, or save it as a file if you need to keep it.
- **Accuracy.** Automatic transcripts can make mistakes, so plan to check names and numbers.

Write down the two or three points that matter for your task, then test a tool on a video you know before you rely on it.

sections.heading: How to get the transcript
sections.body:
Use the same steps every time, and the result is quick to check.

1. Copy the video's link from your browser's address bar.
2. Open [the YouTube transcript tool](https://youtube-transcript.lazur.app/best) and paste the link.
3. Press the button and wait for the text. A short video usually takes about 1 to 3 seconds. Longer videos take longer.
4. Press Copy to put the transcript on your clipboard.

sections.heading: When the transcript is wrong or missing
sections.body:
If the text has errors, compare the part you need with the video. AI transcripts often miss names and some numbers, so check those first.

If the tool says it cannot access the speech, you get that one-sentence message instead of text. Try the link again, and make sure the video opens and plays in your browser. If the same message comes back, try a different video to see whether the problem is with that one video.

sections.heading: Pick the right tool for the job
sections.body:
A transcript is the full text. A summary is a short version of the main points. If you only need the main points, use the [YouTube summarizer](https://youtube-summarizer.lazur.app/) instead.

If you take notes by voice every day, Lazur does this in any app on your Mac. Hold two keys and talk, and it types into whatever app you are in, at [lazur.app](https://www.lazur.app).
